$comment: Selector registry — the one place FWT's brittle UI strings live. Flows reference @keys, never raw copy. testID preferred (copy-proof); text is a Maestro regex matching visible text OR a11y label. Anchors target the seeded 'Standard Tabata' QA fixture (src/qa/fixtures.ts).

app-title.note: TimerList header title (i18n app.title, sentence case) — was 'Workout Timer'/'Free workout timer' before the retired-'Free' cleanup; asserting ONE title on both platforms is the parity regression guard

edit-tabata.note: edit affordance on the seeded Standard Tabata timer. Text = the row's a11y label, which leads with the timer name (was 'Edit Standard Tabata' until 2026-09-10, defect workout-timer-20260809-1: Voice Control matches the accessible name against the words a user can SEE, and the row prints the name first)

stop-confirm.note: confirm button in the system stop alert

send-feedback.note: Settings 'Send feedback' row (i18n about.feedback) — opens the canonical feedback sheet

feedback-bug-option.note: feedback sheet type option (i18n feedback.type.bug). Trailing .* matches the iOS merged a11y label — the card's Pressable sets accessibilityLabel `${title}. ${desc}`, so a bare full-match never hits (the documented iOS card-merge convention)

create-new.note: the timer-list create affordance (i18n timerList.createNew) — opens the editor with a blank EMPTY_TIMER (valid defaults, so Save succeeds with just a name). Used by the T4 survival flow.

name-input.note: the editor name TextInput (i18n editor.nameA11y). A real RN TextInput — in the a11y tree on both platforms.

survival-timer.note: T4 survival marker — a created timer name absent from the seed, so assertNot holds before create and assert can only pass if the new timer persisted. .* for the iOS merged card a11y label.

upgrade-timer.note: T5 upgrade-harness marker — a timer name absent from the QA seed, written by the LAST-RELEASED binary so the assert run can prove it survived installing HEAD over it. Distinct from @survival-timer so a failure names which harness wrote the datum.

sound-work-row.note: the Exercise-start sound DrilldownRow a11y label (default style Voice) — `label: value`

sound-style-chime.note: a style option that only exists inside the SoundStyleSheet (no row shows it by default) — proves the sheet opened

sound-style-bell.note: the style the flow picks; sheet stays open (audition semantics), Back closes

sound-work-row-bell.note: the settings row after the pick — the Tier-2 outcome proof the spoke wrote through

edit-climbing.note: edit button on the seeded climbing timer (fixtures qa-hangboard) — sources the store climbing screenshot slot. Name-first for the same reason as @edit-tabata (was 'Edit Climbing Hangboard')

edit-sequence.note: edit button on the seeded custom-sequence timer (fixtures qa-sequence, 2026-10-17) — opens the sequence editor with its named interval list. Name-first like @edit-tabata.

sequence-interval.note: a named interval row inside the sequence editor (fixtures qa-sequence) — proves the editor rendered the interval list, not the classic sliders. The FIRST interval, not the third: on a 16:9 Android phone the third row sits below the fold and the assert failed (2026-10-17)

start-hangboard.note: start control on the seeded climbing timer (fixtures qa-hangboard: 7s on / 3s off) — the store-preview journey runs it because its intervals flip every few seconds on their own, so the video shows real phase changes without a Skip tap

start-sequence.note: start control on the seeded custom sequence (fixtures qa-sequence) — the store-preview journey shows a named interval running as the phase

skip.note: the running-workout Skip control (i18n workout.skip). The preview journey uses it only to cut the get-ready / warm-up phases short; a retried (double) tap there still lands on a work phase, so it is safe

phase-get-ready.note: the initial-countdown phase label (i18n workout.phase.initial_countdown) — proves the workout screen is up before the preview journey skips the countdown

phase-rest.note: the rest phase label (i18n workout.phase.rest), full-match — the preview journey waits for a real work→rest flip on the hangboard timer

phase-swings.note: a named interval shown AS the phase while the Kettlebell Circuit sequence runs (fixtures qa-sequence) — the preview journey's proof that sequences speak their interval names
